title: Chicken Caesar Salad
subtitle: Grilled chicken with romaine, anchovy dressing, and croutons
excerpt: Cos lettuce with a punchy anchovy and Parmesan dressing, golden croutons, and sliced grilled chicken breast. One of the most popular salads in the world, done properly.

recipe.sourceNotes: The Caesar salad was created in 1924 by Caesar Cardini, an Italian-born restaurateur working in Tijuana, Mexico, at his restaurant Caesar's. The original dressing was made tableside and contained Worcestershire sauce, coddled egg, lemon juice, olive oil, and Parmesan, with no anchovies. Anchovies were added by Cardini's brother Alex and became the standard version used by virtually every restaurant. The original did not contain chicken; it was added in American restaurants as the salad spread in the 1950s and 1960s. The salad became the most popular restaurant salad in the United States and subsequently in Britain, where it appears on almost every pub and restaurant menu. The dressing's intensity comes from the anchovies and the Parmesan working together to create a deeply savoury, umami-rich base.

content.text: The dressing should be bold and intensely savoury. Taste it before dressing the salad and adjust: it needs enough anchovy, lemon, and Parmesan to stand up to the neutral lettuce. The croutons should be deeply golden and crisp; pale, soft croutons are not worth eating. Rest the chicken for 5 minutes before slicing so the juices do not run out.

items.preparation: torn into rough cubes for croutons

content.text: Make the dressing: whisk together the anchovies, garlic, lemon juice, mustard, Worcestershire sauce, and a pinch of salt. Whisk in 4 tablespoons of olive oil until emulsified. Stir in the Parmesan. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Toss the bread cubes in 2 tablespoons of olive oil, salt, and pepper. Fry or bake at 200 C for 10 to 12 minutes until deeply golden and crisp.
Season the chicken with salt and pepper. Heat the vegetable oil in a pan over high heat. Cook the chicken for 5 to 6 minutes per side until golden and cooked through. Rest for 5 minutes, then slice.
Toss the lettuce with most of the dressing. Divide between plates. Top with sliced chicken and croutons. Drizzle with remaining dressing. Scatter with extra Parmesan and black pepper.
